name: Automatic dishwasher detergents
governing_basis: GB 14930.1-2022 (China; National food safety standard - Detergents), Type B: detergents for tableware and food-contact tools, equipment, packaging, and containers. Total arsenic binds the GB 14930.1 Type B species-specific ceiling; Pb, Cd, and tHg are bounded by GB 14930.1's grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg sum). Basis: total content in the product as placed on the market.
native_basis_label: total heavy-metal content in product as placed on the market (mg/kg product)
scope_note: Machine dishwashing detergents (powder, gel, tablets, pods) that clean tableware in an automatic dishwasher. GB 14930.1 Type B (food-contact-article cleaning) governs the product class.

Pb.basis: grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling, product as placed on market (GB 14930.1 <=1.0 mg/kg, sum of Pb+Cd+Hg+... as Pb)
Pb.label: Bounded by the GB 14930.1 grouped heavy-metals ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg as Pb, sum of heavy metals). Lead is a member of the summed group, so it is individually bounded <=1.0 mg/kg; a conservative per-species interpretation of the sovereign grouped limit.

tAs.basis: total arsenic, product as placed on the market (mg/kg)
tAs.label: GB 14930.1-2022 Type B total-arsenic ceiling for detergents used on tableware and food-contact articles (5.0 mg/kg). The stricter Type A ceiling (3.0 mg/kg) governs detergents applied directly to food (washing produce), a different use, and is a same-instrument scope sibling, not a missed stricter limit.

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for detergents or cleaning products; GB 14930.1 and every consumer-chemical trace-metal instrument regulate TOTAL arsenic (see the tAs cell), which bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). Inorganic arsenic is a dietary/water speciation with no separate cleaning-product instrument. No routed occurrence source measured or speciated inorganic arsenic in these products.
iAs.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-arsenic ceiling (GB 14930.1 Type B, 5.0 mg/kg); no inorganic-arsenic limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII; US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada; Germany BfR
iAs.cross_sourced: parent tAs published (GB 14930.1 Type B) + credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no iAs cleaning-product limit); occurrence corpus (zhang2010; ecetoc1992) measured no arsenic speciation
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic screen by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market; reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation only if total arsenic approaches the ceiling.

Cd.basis: grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling, product as placed on market (GB 14930.1 <=1.0 mg/kg, sum of Pb+Cd+Hg+... as Pb)
Cd.label: Bounded by the GB 14930.1 grouped heavy-metals ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg as Pb). Cadmium is a member of the summed group and is individually bounded <=1.0 mg/kg; conservative per-species interpretation of the sovereign grouped limit.

tHg.basis: grouped heavy-metals-as-Pb ceiling, product as placed on market (GB 14930.1 <=1.0 mg/kg, sum of Pb+Cd+Hg+... as Pb)
tHg.label: Bounded by the GB 14930.1 grouped heavy-metals ceiling (<=1.0 mg/kg as Pb). Mercury is a member of the summed group and is individually bounded <=1.0 mg/kg; conservative per-species interpretation of the sovereign grouped limit.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation or migration pathway in a detergent formulation; it is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation. Every mercury instrument that touches this product class regulates total mercury (GB 14930.1's grouped heavy-metals ceiling, see the tHg cell), which bounds any organomercury fraction. No routed occurrence source measured or speciated methylmercury in these products.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-mercury (grouped heavy-metals) ceiling (GB 14930.1, <=1.0 mg/kg as Pb); no methylmercury limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII; US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada; Germany BfR
MeHg.cross_sourced: parent tHg published (grouped GB 14930.1) + credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no MeHg cleaning-product limit); occurrence corpus screened, no organomercury speciation reported
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by CV-AAS or ICP-MS; no reflex methylmercury speciation defined for cleaning products (no formation pathway).

Ni.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market (acid digestion).
Ni.escalation_rule: Nickel is a confirmed dermal sensitizer and is measured in household cleaning products (zhang2010 dish soap; ecetoc1992 dish/all-purpose/specialty cleaners). No jurisdiction sets a numeric total-nickel maximum for cleaning products, so certification screens total nickel and escalates a lot above the running category control band to ALARA review rather than pass/failing on an invented number.
Ni.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis. A drinking-water or article-migration nickel value is a different basis and is not read across.

Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
Al.escalation_rule: Aluminium is Tier-2 (low toxicity by the oral/dermal routes at cleaning-product exposure) and may be a functional mineral ingredient (alumina abrasives, aluminosilicate builders). No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product aluminium maximum. Screen total aluminium; a lot outside the functional-ingredient expectation triggers ingredient review.
Al.rationale: No sovereign ML; potential functional-ingredient source means a not-material claim would be false. Screen, do not publish a number.

Cr-total.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on the product as placed on market.
Cr-total.escalation_rule: Total chromium is measured in cleaning products (zhang2010; ecetoc1992). No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product chromium maximum. Screen total chromium and reflex Cr(VI) speciation where total chromium is elevated or the formulation is oxidizing/acidic.
Cr-total.rationale: Present in the occurrence corpus; no sovereign ML in a consumer-chemical total-content basis.

Cr-VI.reference_method: Hexavalent chromium by IC-ICP-MS with alkaline extraction (US EPA 3060A / 7199) on oxidizing or acidic formulations.
Cr-VI.escalation_rule: Cr(VI) is measured in some consumer cleaning products (ecetoc1992) and oxidizing/acidic chemistries can stabilize it. No jurisdiction sets a cleaning-product Cr(VI) maximum. Reflex Cr(VI) speciation on oxidizing/acidic formulations and where total chromium is elevated; escalate a positive Cr(VI) result to ALARA review.
Cr-VI.rationale: Measured in the corpus; a real hazard on oxidizing chemistries; no sovereign number, so a method + escalation rule is published rather than an invented threshold.

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin has no source in a detergent/dish-cleaning formulation (no tinplate or canned-food pathway). Organotin is a DISTINCT species (biocide/stabiliser) restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 and is screened separately where a formulation could carry it; it does not bound, and is not bounded by, this inorganic-tin cell. No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-tin limit for cleaning products, and no routed occurrence source measured tin (the zhang2010 ten-metal panel excludes tin).
Sn.regulatory_basis: No inorganic-tin limit for cleaning products in any jurisdiction; organotin covered separately under REACH Annex XVII entry 20
Sn.jurisdictions_checked: CN GB 14930.1; CN NMPA 2015; EU 10/2011; EU REACH Annex XVII (entry 20 organotin); US EPA Safer Choice; Green Seal GS-8; CA SB 258; NY Household Cleaner Disclosure; Health Canada
Sn.cross_sourced: credible-ML register checked 2026-08-13 (no inorganic-Sn cleaning-product limit; only organotin restriction, a distinct species); occurrence corpus measured no tin (zhang2010 ten-metal panel excludes Sn)
Sn.reference_method: Periodic ICP-MS inorganic-tin verification; organotin (DBT/DOT/TBT as Sn) screened separately by GC-ICP-MS where a biocidal-organotin pathway is plausible.

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default, consumer-chemical form; native basis = total heavy-metal content in product as placed on market, mg/kg; no cross-basis min)
